q: All the following are true in haemophilia EXCEPT:
o: It affects males and females equally
e: Haemophilia is X-linked, so boys are affected.

q: The following are features of von Willebrand disease EXCEPT:
e: Von Willebrand disease is usually autosomal dominant.

q: All are features of haemophilia A EXCEPT:
o: Males and females are equally affected
Haemarthrosis can be the presenting feature

q: A 1-month-old bleeds after circumcision; his older brother has the same problem. The expected test result is:
e: Haemophilia: a prolonged APTT, with a normal prothrombin time and bleeding time.

q: A prolonged bleeding time is NOT seen in:
e: Haemophilia has a normal bleeding time.

q: Regarding ITP in children, all are true EXCEPT:
o: Steroids are one mode of therapy
It often follows a viral infection
Intracranial haemorrhage is a rare complication
e: About 80% recover; splenectomy is rarely needed.

q: Thrombocytopenia is present in all of the following EXCEPT:
e: Henoch–Schönlein purpura is a vasculitis with normal platelets.

o: PT and bleeding time are both abnormal
Factor IX deficiency is haemophilia B
e: Haemophilia B (factor IX deficiency) is also called Christmas disease.

o: It is caused by antiplatelet antibodies
e: ITP is caused by IgG autoantibodies against platelets.

e: With skin bleeding only, the child is observed.
